gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-esteban: Bold and tube-like in Tilt Neon, every stroke the same gauge, with a splayed c to finish it off. And Esteban takes over below as a serif with a softly varied stroke, its lowercase generous enough to carry long paragraphs without tiring.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-halant: Halant reads as a sturdy classic serif, with a faint thick-thin shift and outward-pointing terminals under its tall lowercase. Tilt Neon above it stays flat and unmodulated, so bump the heading up a size.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-headland-one: Tilt Neon's tube-like stroke never tapers or swells anywhere. Headland One follows as a text serif with fuller stems and slimmer links, so a long page moves along at a dignified, unhurried pace.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-hedvig-letters-serif: Tilt Neon brings a splayed c and a stroke that never pinches or swells, big and bold up top. Hedvig Letters Serif sits underneath as a text serif with open curves and a sturdy body, giving the page a firm, steady footing.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa reads sturdy and large, its tall lowercase and spilling counters making words feel generous on the page. But Tilt Neon above it holds every stroke at one gauge, so a long passage drifts down in a gentle ebb and flow.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-marcellus-sc: Tilt Neon is cut like rod stock, with horizontals and verticals of identical thickness and a large x-height that dominates the line. Marcellus SC, a serif, offers the mellow counterweight.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-montagu-slab: A splayed c terminal and a tube-like stroke with no brush swell define Tilt Neon. Montagu Slab, a text serif, answers with robust downstrokes and slender turns, and that solid readability is what makes the combination work.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-ovo: Chunky, tube-like and unshaded, Tilt Neon leads the way. Ovo, a serif with moderate contrast and a tall middle band, then carries a long passage along easily, its curve terminals leaving plenty of space.
gen-gf-turret-road-fs-karma: Round forms like open parentheses, drawn with one pen-like line. Karma, a classic serif, follows with terminals that finish well clear of the stem, so a long passage glides along without snagging the eye.
gen-gf-turret-road-fs-literata: Literata is a classic serif with sturdy thin lines, slightly heavier thick ones, and wide, unclosed mouths on its curves. And Turret Road, with its wire-like monoline skeleton, feels like a bold, commanding stranger standing beside it.
